question: At an 85th-percentile approach speed of 45 mph, from how far in advance should the two primary signal faces be continuously visible, and what treatment is recommended if that view is unavailable?
model_answer: Direct Answer: The two primary signal faces should be continuously visible from at least the minimum sight distance given in Table 4D-2 in advance of (measured to) the stop line; however, the table excerpt in the evidence provided lists distances only up to 35 mph (325 feet), so the specific value for 45 mph cannot be stated from this evidence. If approaching traffic does not have a continuous view of at least two signal faces for that distance, the recommended treatment is to install a warning sign (see Section 2C.35) to warn approaching traffic of the signal. Separately, at 45 mph or higher, signal backplates should be used on all signal faces facing the approach. Guidance (recommended): - The two primary signal faces required as a minimum for each approach should be continuously visible from a point at least the minimum sight distance provided in Table 4D-2 in advance of and measured to the stop line, unless precluded by a physical obstruction or another signalized location within this range. (The table excerpt available here covers only 20–35 mph, so the 45-mph distance is not shown in the provided evidence.) - If approaching traffic does not have a continuous view of at least two signal faces for at least the minimum sight distance shown in Table 4D-2, a sign (see Section 2C.35) should be installed to warn approaching traffic of the traffic control signal. - If the posted or statutory speed limit or the 85th-percentile speed on an approach is 45 mph or higher, signal backplates should be used on all of the signal faces that face the approach. - On approaches with speeds of 45 mph or higher, for new or reconstructed installations: primary signal faces for through traffic should be provided per Table 4D-1; overhead faces should be located approximately over the center of each through lane when their number equals the number of through lanes; primary faces for mandatory turn lanes should be located overhead over the center of each such lane; all primary signal faces should be on the far side of the intersection; supplemental faces should be considered for visibility behind large vehicles; and all signal faces should have backplates. Citations: - Section 4D.06 Guidance §5 (p.670) - Section 4D.06 Guidance §6 (p.670) - Section 4D.06 Guidance §17 (p.671) - Section 4D.05 Guidance §7 (p.668)
gold_answer: They should be continuously visible from at least 460 feet in advance of the stop line. If at least two faces are not continuously visible for that distance, a warning sign should be installed for approaching traffic.
